name: Geometric probability
formula: P = \frac{\text{measure of favourable region}}{\text{measure of whole region}}
whenToUse: Points or numbers are chosen uniformly at random from an interval, square or other region. Draw the region and compare lengths or areas.
example: Choose $x$ and $y$ independently and uniformly from $[0, 1]$. The region $|x - y| \ge \frac{1}{3}$ is two corner triangles with legs $\frac{2}{3}$, of total area $\frac{4}{9}$, so $P\left(|x - y| < \frac{1}{3}\right) = \frac{5}{9}$.
pitfall: Two random numbers give a SQUARE of outcomes, not an interval. Sketch it: most errors come from mis-drawing the boundary lines.
